method: The plan is fixed by the target and the two legs you do not leave open. Each known leg is its distance times its pace: the swim in metres divided by 100 times the swim pace, the run in kilometres times the run pace, and the bike in kilometres divided by its speed times 3600 to get seconds. Both transitions are subtracted from the target first, so the open leg takes whatever remains and must still be a positive time: the target minus T1, T2 and the two known legs. When the bike is open its average speed is the bike distance divided by that remaining time, and the page reports it in km/h; when the run is open its pace is the remaining time divided by the run distance in km; when the swim is open its pace is the remaining time divided by the swim distance in hundreds of metres. The four course presets fill the standard distances - sprint 750 m, 20 km and 5 km; Olympic 1.5 km, 40 km and 10 km; 70.3 1.9 km, 90 km and 21.0975 km; Ironman 3.8 km, 180 km and 42.195 km - and leave the paces alone, so the same target can be re-costed on a longer course. Times accept h:mm:ss, mm:ss or plain seconds with at most one decimal place, and are range-checked rather than clamped: the target must fall between 5 minutes and 36 hours, each transition between 0 and 2 hours, swim distance between 50 and 10000 m, bike distance between 1 and 500 km, run distance between 1 and 100 km, swim pace between 0:30 and 20:00 per 100 m, run pace between 2:00 and 30:00 per km, and a typed bike speed between 5 and 100 km/h. A solved leg outside those same ranges is refused instead of printed, so a target that would demand 100.8 km/h on the bike or a 0:15 swim pace says so. The splits are averages for the whole leg: no wind, gradient, drafting, wetsuit, sighting or pacing strategy is modelled, and the transitions are the fixed times entered rather than estimates. Times are displayed rounded to the nearest second and the solved speed to one decimal, so a shown split can differ from the underlying value by up to half a second. Everything is computed locally with arithmetic on the numbers typed: no network access, uploads, accounts or storage.

sources.title: World Triathlon competition distances: sprint 750 m swim, 20 km bike, 5 km run; standard distance 1.5 km, 40 km, 10 km; middle distance 1.9 km, 90 km, 21.0975 km; long distance 3.8 km, 180 km, 42.195 km.
Pace convention used by race results: swim pace is quoted per 100 m and run pace per kilometre, each as time per unit distance.
Arithmetic: leg time is distance times pace, the open leg is the target minus both transitions and the two known legs, and average speed is distance divided by time.
